newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir going on series of vacations - minister.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir going on series of vacations - minister.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad is taking a series of short vacations in between official visits to a number of European states and not a month-long sabatical, Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik said on Wednesday.
Ling said Mahathir is scheduled to visit London and a number of eastern European countries to discuss Malaysia's new technology zone, the Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC), and other bilateral issues.

"PM is going to London on some work on the MSC and then he will take leave...for a few days. He is also scheduled to visit Poland, Russia. In between he'll take some leave," Ling told reporters after attending a weekly Cabinet meeting.
Ling was responding to reports that Mahathir will be going on an unusually long vacation starting this month.
A senior government source said on Wednesday that the 71-year-old leader, who is currently on an official visit to African nations, could be gone from the end of May.

The source said that during Mahathir's absence, Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim was expected to run the country. Earlier, speculation about Mahathir's unusually long-leave raised questions among some political analysts about his health.
But the government source said: "This has nothing to do with his health." Mahathir had a heart operation in 1989.
Ling played down Mahathir's impending leave, saying the premier only wanted to stay in Europe between the state visits to save the trouble of adjusting to different time zones.
"Instead of flying all the way back here..then all the way back there and the time (zone) change again, I think it's quite wise...to stay in the same time zone," he said.
Ling said Mahathir, who keeps a full schedule, also needed a rest.
